theorem.statement: Under the present certificate grammar and checker, the answer to the proof-carrying compiler question is negative.  For every integer \(k\geq 1\), there is an explicit finite acyclic target grounding and compact equality-query description whose combined pre-incidence input size is \(O(k)\), whose target ground graph is edgeless and hence has treewidth \(w=0\), and which has binary variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_{k+1}\), no intervention, target event \(B=\{X_1=X_{k+1}\}\), a fair supported row at \(X_1\), and the unsupported binary row \(rstar\) at \(X_{k+1}\).  The row \(rstar\) is directly event-relevant and the replayed target polynomial is the nontrivial constant \(F=1/2\), while the mandated \(Ictx\) contains exactly \(2^k\) event-consistent complete target-assignment records.  Consequently, every compiler that outputs an \(Ictx\) accepted by \(Check\) has time and output length \(\Omega(2^k)\).  Thus no bound polynomial in the explicit grounding size and exponential only in \(w\) is possible for this exhaustive assignment-level grammar.  This conclusion does not rule out a width-sensitive compiler after replacement of \(Ictx\) and \(Check\) by a compact circuit-level incidence grammar and checker.
theorem.proof_tex: This is exactly the claim of thm:assignment-incidence-obstructs-width-compiler; apply thm:assignment-incidence-obstructs-width-compiler.
